key_insight: Optimized surface-code memory on a cloud-accessible IBM processor suppressed logical errors as the protected code distance increased from 3 to 6.
engineering_relevance: Coordinating readout, reset, and data-qubit echo operations can improve logical memory performance on current superconducting hardware.
method: Test rotated surface-code memory across placements on an IBM Nighthawk r2 processor.
Combine short readout, fused measurement and reset, and XX echo during ancilla readout.
Evaluate distance scaling with maximum-likelihood decoding and memory experiments up to 150 rounds.
evidence_signal: With the other code distance fixed, increasing the protected distance from 3 to 6 reduced per-round logical errors from 0.53% to 0.24% in Z memory and from 0.52% to 0.22% in X memory.
watch_item: The distance advantage weakened in longer memory experiments, while long-lived correlations suggested a possible persistent error component.
paper_title: Demonstration of Logical Error Suppression in a Surface Code Memory on a Cloud-Accessible IBM Superconducting Processor
